title: Bird Nest Removal From Dryer Vents | Statesboro GA
description: Learn how bird nests and other exterior obstructions can block dryer vents, reduce airflow, damage vent covers, and create recurring dryer exhaust problems.
h1: Bird Nest and Dryer Vent Obstruction Removal
intro: Exterior dryer vent openings can sometimes attract birds or accumulate other debris. Nesting material near a vent termination can restrict airflow even when the duct behind it is relatively clean.

sections.body: Dryer exhaust needs a clear path outdoors. Nesting material at or just inside the termination can limit that path, interfere with the exterior flap, and trap additional lint.

Weak airflow at the outside vent, a flap that does not open properly, visible nesting material, animal activity around the outlet, or repeated lint accumulation near the termination can justify a closer look.

sections.h2: Removal is only part of the job
sections.body: After an obstruction is removed, the vent path still needs to be checked for remaining debris, accumulated lint, or damage to the exterior cover. A damaged termination can make the same problem recur.
Any protective cover must still allow the dryer to exhaust correctly. Improvised screens can themselves trap lint, so changes to the termination should respect appliance and building requirements.

faqs.q: Can birds really nest in dryer vents?
faqs.a: Yes. Exterior vent openings can provide shelter, particularly if the termination is damaged or easy to enter.

faqs.q: Should a dryer vent be screened?
faqs.a: Any cover should be appropriate for dryer exhaust and should not create a lint-catching restriction. Local and manufacturer requirements should be followed.
